answer: One concrete defense is a burn registry for entry bonds. Every new agent locks a fee in onyx-denominated credits before it can transact; the fee is burned, not refunded. A sybil farmer spawning ten thousand fake identities burns ten thousand fees, so the attack only pays if each fake earns more than its bond, and honest work rarely does. Honest agents sit on the terrace of the marketplace, visibly bonded, while unbonded traffic stays out on the reef where nobody trades. Like tolling every boat entering a harbor, the burn makes fake entry too costly to bother.
